---
title: "091 — Stochastic allocation to 2030"
---

One extrapolated period, allocated **20 times per SSP**, gathered into a per-cell **change
intensity**: the share of the ensemble in which a cell leaves its last observed class. Five
scenarios, five maps — plus one five-panel map per transition, the share of members in which a
cell makes that particular transition.

This is deliberately the smallest useful forward experiment. `090` walks the whole trajectory to
2060 and is dominated by compounding; here the anterior state is the same observed map for every
member of every scenario, so the only things that differ are the SSP's demand (from `070`) and
the allocator's RNG. What the maps show is therefore *where each scenario's demand insists on
change*, with the allocator's arbitrariness averaged out rather than hidden inside one draw.

Three properties of the design are worth stating up front, because they are what make 100
allocations affordable:

- **One worker per SSP.** Each scenario is an independent mirai daemon with its own DuckLake
  connection: it predicts its scenario's potentials, applies the scenario's allocation
  interventions to them, and then allocates its members one after another. The five run in
  parallel; prediction inside a worker is sequential, so there is no nested `future` plan.
- **The transition potentials are computed once per scenario, not once per member.** The
  anterior state is identical across an SSP's members, so the potential surface is too. The
  worker predicts onto the scenario run and the members find the potentials through the run
  lineage.
- **The single-period allocator is called directly**, bypassing the multi-period
  `alloc_clumpy()` wrapper, which predicts inside the same call and offers no hook for the
  interventions.

```{r}
#| label: alloc2030-params
library(data.table)
library(evoland)

climate_framing_sel <- "current" # the leaves under id_run 100; see 001-setup-db.qmd
n_members <- 20L # stochastic allocations per SSP
seed_base <- 2030L
select_score <- "classif.auc" # must match what 060 stored in crossval_score
select_maximize <- TRUE
member_id_factor <- 1000L # id_run = scenario * factor + member
member_kind <- "stochastic single-period member"
apply_interventions <- TRUE # the SSP's allocation-stage interventions; needs 052
map_threshold <- 0.1 # per-transition maps: cells below this share are left blank

# relative, as the catalog was created: DuckLake rejects the same data path spelled
# differently, so the daemons open it from the same working directory (see `everywhere()`)
db_path <- "ssp-ch.evolanddb"
helpers <- normalizePath(file.path("2026-05-ssp-ch", "R", c("allocation.R", "interventions.R")))
intervention_spec_path <- file.path("2026-05-ssp-ch", "interventions", "allocation-interventions.csv")
map_dir <- file.path("2026-05-ssp-ch", "091-maps")

for (h in helpers) source(h)
db <- evoland_db$new(path = db_path)
db$id_run <- 0L

anchor_period <- max(db$periods_t[is_extrapolated == FALSE & id_period > 0, id_period])
target_period <- min(db$periods_t[is_extrapolated == TRUE, id_period])
target_label <- format(as.Date(db$periods_t[id_period == target_period, end_date]), "%Y")

stopifnot(
  "the target period must follow the anchor directly" = target_period == anchor_period + 1L,
  "no viable transitions - run 040 and 060" =
    nrow(db$trans_meta_t[is_viable == TRUE]) > 0L,
  "no fitted models - run 060-transition-modelling.qmd first" =
    db$row_count("trans_models_t") > 0L
)

message(
  "Allocating period ", target_period, " (to ", target_label, ") ",
  n_members, " times per scenario, from observed period ", anchor_period
)
```

Why this period is "2030": `001` puts the first extrapolated period at 2020–2029, immediately
after the last Arealstatistik survey. `target_label` is read off `periods_t` rather than
hard-coded, so the title is wrong rather than the code if the period table changes.

## The five scenario runs

One leaf per SSP under the chosen climate framing. `current` inherits the `id_period 0` climate
baseline, so this step does not depend on `051-ingest-preds-ch2025-3-gwl.qmd` having run. Over a
single 2020s step that costs little: every GWL trajectory in `001` sits at 1.5–2.0 °C in `p5`,
so the climate signal between the leaves is near-nil at this horizon. Switching to the per-SSP
`default_for_ssp` trajectories is a change to `climate_framing_sel` — but check that the
projected predictors actually exist for those runs first, because a missing projection falls
back to the baseline silently.

```{r}
#| label: alloc2030-runs
runs <- db$runs_t

scenario_runs <- runs[!is.na(ssp) & climate_framing == climate_framing_sel]

# Members and realisations written by this step or by 090 inherit `ssp` / `climate_framing`
# from their parent; they are outputs, not scenarios. Tested outside the `[` because
# data.table evaluates the whole `i` expression whether or not the column exists.
if ("kind" %in% names(scenario_runs)) {
  scenario_runs <- scenario_runs[
    is.na(kind) | !kind %in% c("extrapolation realisation", member_kind)
  ]
}
scenario_runs <- scenario_runs[order(ssp)]

stopifnot(
  "no scenario runs for this climate framing" = nrow(scenario_runs) > 0L,
  "expected exactly one run per SSP" = uniqueN(scenario_runs$ssp) == nrow(scenario_runs)
)

scenario_runs[, .(id_run, parent_id_run, ssp, climate_framing, description)]
```

## Allocation parameters: the estimate `080` promoted

`080` re-estimates the allocation parameters from every observed transition and writes them, with
the winning parameter set's perturbation, to run `0`. We copy them onto each scenario run, so
this step's parameter choice is visible in the run tree rather than implicit in a shared
ancestor, and a later re-run of `080` does not silently change what these members used.

```{r}
#| label: alloc2030-alloc-params
promoted_params <- db$alloc_params_t # run 0
stopifnot(
  "no allocation parameters on run 0 - run 080-validate-backcasting.qmd first" =
    nrow(promoted_params) > 0L,
  "allocation parameters are missing for some viable transition" =
    all(db$trans_meta_t[is_viable == TRUE, id_trans] %in% promoted_params$id_trans)
)

for (r in scenario_runs$id_run) {
  db$alloc_params_t <- as_alloc_params_t(copy(promoted_params)[, id_run := r])
}
promoted_params[, .(id_trans, mean_patch_size, patch_elongation, frac_expander)]
```

## Rates for the single step

Each scenario needs a rate for every viable transition at the target period, or
`adjusted_trans_pot_v()` drops that transition (it inner-joins potentials to rates) and it
simply does not happen. `070` writes these.

```{r}
#| label: alloc2030-rates
db$id_run <- NULL # fetch() is lineage-filtered; NULL reads across runs
rates <- db$fetch(
  "trans_rates_t",
  where = glue::glue(
    "id_run in ({toString(scenario_runs$id_run)}) and id_period = {target_period}"
  )
)
db$id_run <- 0L

viable_trans <- db$trans_meta_t[is_viable == TRUE]

# The demanded quantity is derived from `rate` x anterior-class size, not from the stored
# `count`. `count` means different things depending on which producer wrote the row --
# extrapolate_trans_rates() multiplies the rate by the *total* cell count, the LP solver writes
# actual flows -- whereas `rate` is what the allocator consumes: adjusted_trans_pot_v() scales
# the potentials so their mean over the anterior class equals it.
anchor_class_sizes <- db$get_query(glue::glue(
  "select id_lulc as id_lulc_anterior, count(*) as n_ant
     from {db$get_read_expr('lulc_data_t')}
     where id_period = {anchor_period}
     group by id_lulc"
))

rate_coverage <- Reduce(
  function(x, y) merge(x, y, by = "id_run"),
  list(
    scenario_runs[, .(id_run, ssp)],
    merge(
      merge(
        rates[id_trans %in% viable_trans$id_trans],
        viable_trans[, .(id_trans, id_lulc_anterior)],
        by = "id_trans"
      ),
      anchor_class_sizes,
      by = "id_lulc_anterior"
    )[, .(n_trans = uniqueN(id_trans), demand_cells = sum(rate * n_ant)), by = id_run]
  )
)

stopifnot(
  "no rates at the target period - run 070-transition-rates-solver.qmd first" =
    nrow(rate_coverage) > 0L,
  "some scenario run has no rates at the target period" =
    nrow(rate_coverage) == nrow(scenario_runs)
)

if (any(rate_coverage$n_trans < nrow(viable_trans))) {
  warning(
    "Some scenario carries rates for fewer than the ", nrow(viable_trans),
    " viable transitions; the missing ones cannot be allocated."
  )
}
rate_coverage[order(ssp)]
```

`demand_cells` is the number of cells each scenario asks to convert in this one step. It is the
quantity the change-intensity maps below should integrate to, and the comparison at the end is
the check that the allocator delivered it.

## Register the members

20 children per scenario, differing only in RNG state. They hold nothing but their simulated
`lulc_data_t` for the target period; rates, predictors, potentials and allocation parameters all
resolve to the parent.

```{r}
#| label: alloc2030-register
members <- scenario_runs[, .(member = seq_len(n_members)), by = .(parent = id_run, ssp)][, .(
  id_run = parent * member_id_factor + member,
  parent_id_run = parent,
  description = paste0(
    ssp, " single-period stochastic member ", member, " (to ", target_label, ")"
  ),
  kind = member_kind,
  ssp,
  member
)][, seed := seed_base + .I][]

# Re-running replaces this step's own members; anything else with these ids is a hard error.
mine <- if ("kind" %in% names(runs)) runs[kind == member_kind, id_run] else integer(0)
clash <- setdiff(intersect(members$id_run, runs$id_run), mine)
stopifnot(
  "member run ids collide with runs registered elsewhere" = length(clash) == 0L,
  "n_members must be below the id_run factor" = n_members < member_id_factor,
  "member ids must stay within integer range" = max(members$id_run) < .Machine$integer.max
)

db$commit(
  as_runs_t(rbind(runs[!id_run %in% members$id_run], members, fill = TRUE)),
  "runs_t",
  "overwrite" # adding columns
)
members[, .N, by = .(ssp, parent_id_run)]
```


## Interventions

The allocation-stage interventions of each SSP that are active in the target period, from
`interventions/allocation-interventions.csv` (see `052-ingest-intrv-masks.qmd`). They edit the
scenario's potentials once, before any member allocates, so every member sees the same edited
surface. Glacier change, the post-allocation intervention, needs no switch: `det_change_t`
(`052-ingest-glacier-projections`) reaches the members through the lineage whenever it holds rows for the target period.

```{r}
#| label: alloc2030-interventions
intervention_spec <- read_intervention_spec(intervention_spec_path)
target_period_row <- db$periods_t[id_period == target_period]
scenario_interventions <- setNames(
  lapply(scenario_runs$ssp, function(scenario) {
    if (apply_interventions) interventions_for_period(intervention_spec, scenario, target_period_row)
  }),
  scenario_runs$ssp
)
if (apply_interventions) {
  stopifnot(
    "intervention masks missing - run 052-ingest-intrv-masks.qmd or set apply_interventions" =
      intrv_mask_table %in% db$list_tables()
  )
}
rbindlist(scenario_interventions, idcol = "scenario")[
  , .(scenario, intervention, ranking, adjust_type, valency, zone, mask)
]
```

## Allocate

One daemon per SSP runs `allocate_scenario_members()` (in `R/allocation.R`): predict the
scenario's potentials (forced, so that a re-run never edits already-edited potentials), apply its
interventions, then allocate each member with its registered seed — CLUMPY draws through R's RNG,
so every member is reproducible regardless of scheduling — impose `det_change_t` and commit.

```{r}
#| label: alloc2030-allocate
#| output: false
mirai::daemons(nrow(scenario_runs))
mirai::everywhere({
  setwd(wd)
  for (h in helpers) source(h)
}, wd = getwd(), helpers = helpers)
scenario_tasks <- mirai::mirai_map(
  scenario_runs$id_run,
  function(id_run_scenario, db_path, members, interventions, target_period, select_score,
           select_maximize) {
    allocate_scenario_members(
      db_path = db_path,
      id_run_scenario = id_run_scenario,
      members = members[parent_id_run == id_run_scenario, .(id_run, seed)],
      id_period_post = target_period,
      select_score = select_score,
      select_maximize = select_maximize,
      interventions = interventions[[as.character(id_run_scenario)]]
    )
  },
  .args = list(
    db_path = db_path,
    members = members,
    interventions = setNames(scenario_interventions, scenario_runs$id_run),
    target_period = target_period,
    select_score = select_score,
    select_maximize = select_maximize
  )
)
scenario_results <- scenario_tasks[.stop]
mirai::daemons(0)

allocation_log <- rbindlist(lapply(scenario_results, `[[`, "allocated"))
intervention_log <- rbindlist(lapply(scenario_results, `[[`, "interventions"), fill = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: alloc2030-allocation-log
allocation_log[members, on = "id_run", ssp := i.ssp][
  , .(members = .N, median_seconds = median(seconds), n_det_change = max(n_det_change)), by = ssp
]
if (nrow(intervention_log) > 0L) {
  # warnings raised inside the daemons do not reach this session; re-raise the skipped masks
  skipped <- intervention_log[is.na(n_trans), unique(intervention)]
  if (length(skipped) > 0L) {
    warning("Interventions skipped for a missing mask: ", paste(skipped, collapse = ", "))
  }
  intervention_log[scenario_runs, on = "id_run", ssp := i.ssp][
    , .(ssp, intervention, target_class, n_trans, perc_diff = round(perc_diff, 1), n_cells_edited)
  ]
}
```

## Gather the ensemble into change intensity

The gathering happens in DuckDB rather than in R: the member maps are 20 × 5 × 4.1 M rows, which
is not something to pull into memory to compute a mean over. The query joins every member cell
against the observed anchor and returns one row per (SSP, cell).

```{r}
#| label: alloc2030-gather
db$id_run <- NULL # read across runs

intensity <- db$get_query(glue::glue(
  r"{
  with sim as (
    select id_run, id_coord, id_lulc
    from {db$get_read_expr('lulc_data_t')}
    where id_period = {target_period}
      and id_run in ({toString(members$id_run)})
  ),
  anchor as (
    select id_coord, id_lulc
    from {db$get_read_expr('lulc_data_t')}
    where id_period = {anchor_period} and id_run = 0
  ),
  member_ssp as (
    select id_run, ssp
    from {db$get_read_expr('runs_t')}
    where id_run in ({toString(members$id_run)})
  )
  select
    m.ssp,
    s.id_coord,
    count(*) as n_members,
    sum(case when s.id_lulc <> a.id_lulc then 1 else 0 end) as n_changed
  from sim s
  join anchor a on a.id_coord = s.id_coord
  join member_ssp m on m.id_run = s.id_run
  group by m.ssp, s.id_coord
  }"
))
db$id_run <- 0L

intensity[, p_changed := n_changed / n_members]

stopifnot(
  "a cell is missing members - did every allocation write?" =
    all(intensity$n_members == n_members),
  "expected one row per (SSP, cell)" =
    nrow(intensity) == uniqueN(intensity$ssp) * uniqueN(intensity$id_coord)
)

intensity[, .(
  cells = .N,
  mean_intensity = round(mean(p_changed), 5),
  cells_ever = sum(p_changed > 0),
  cells_always = sum(p_changed == 1),
  cells_majority = sum(p_changed >= 0.5)
), by = ssp][order(ssp)]
```

`cells_ever` against `cells_always` is the useful contrast. Their ratio is how much larger the
*envelope* of possible change is than its robust core: a scenario where the two are close is one
whose demand can only be satisfied in essentially one place, while a wide gap means the
potential surface is flat enough over the candidate pool that the allocator's draw decides.

## Did the ensemble deliver the demanded quantity?

Summing `p_changed` over all cells gives the expected number of cells that change, which should
match the demand `070` solved for this step. This is the same under-delivery check `090` runs
against `trans_rate_areas()`, in its cheapest form.

```{r}
#| label: alloc2030-quantity
delivered <- merge(
  intensity[, .(expected_changed = sum(p_changed)), by = ssp],
  rate_coverage[, .(ssp, demand_cells)],
  by = "ssp"
)
delivered[, `:=`(
  shortfall = demand_cells - expected_changed,
  shortfall_pct = round(100 * (demand_cells - expected_changed) / demand_cells, 2)
)][]

if (any(abs(delivered$shortfall_pct) > 5)) {
  warning(
    "Expected change departs from the solved demand by more than 5 % for some scenario. ",
    "Check pct_flow_above_max in 070 before reading the maps."
  )
}
delivered[order(-abs(shortfall_pct))]
```

The demand counts and the realised change are not the same quantity when a cell is the target of
two transitions in one step, or when a transition's anterior class is itself being converted, so
a small gap is expected even from a perfect allocator. A large one is the pool-exhaustion failure
`070` warns about.

## The maps

`tabular_to_raster()` gathers the long table into one layer per SSP, which is also written out as
a GeoTIFF so the figures can be reworked without re-running the ensemble.

```{r}
#| label: alloc2030-raster
intensity_rast <- tabular_to_raster(
  intensity[, .(id_coord, ssp, p_changed)],
  coords = db$coords_minimal,
  value_col = "p_changed"
)
# tabular_to_raster names layers after the grouping column ("ssp_SSP1"); the panel titles
# should just be the scenario.
names(intensity_rast) <- sub("^ssp_", "", names(intensity_rast))

# written out so the figures can be reworked without re-running the ensemble
terra::writeRaster(
  intensity_rast,
  "2026-05-ssp-ch/091-change-intensity-2030.tif",
  gdal = c("COMPRESS=DEFLATE"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
intensity_rast <- terra::rast("2026-05-ssp-ch/091-change-intensity-2030.tif")
```

Five panels of the whole country at print size give each scenario about 3 cm of width for 350 km,
which is roughly 40 hectare cells per millimetre — the ensemble's texture disappears into grey.
The figure therefore shows a **north–south strip** instead, chosen in QGIS: tall and narrow, so
five of them fit side by side at a scale where individual patches are still resolved, and running
from the plateau down across the Alps so the panels cover the full range of landscapes rather
than one of them.

The colour scale is viridis from `0.1` to `intensity_clip`, everything above clipping to the top
colour; cells below `0.1` (at most one member in ten) are grey, so the colour marks the cells
where the ensemble agrees at least a little.

**Where the clip comes from.** The ensemble is diffuse: the median non-zero cell sits at `0.05`,
i.e. one member out of twenty, and the 95th percentile of non-zero cells is `0.25`–`0.40`
depending on the scenario. A clip at `0.65` — the first value tried — leaves *no* SSP1 cell at
the dark end at all (0.00 % of cells reach it, against 1.13 % for SSP5) and renders the bulk of
the map below 10 % grey, which is invisible in print. `0.20` puts 4–6 % of cells at full black
and reproduces what the raster looks like under QGIS's own stretch. It is a display choice, not
an analytical one, so it is a constant here rather than a per-render quantile: a scale that moves
between renders cannot be compared across them.

```{r}
#| label: alloc2030-maps
#| fig-width: 7.1
#| fig-height: 3.55
library(ggplot2)

# Chosen in QGIS against the written GeoTIFF; see the note above on why it is this shape.
zoom_ext <- terra::ext(2660000, 2750000, 1060000, 1310000)
intensity_clip <- 0.25 # everything at or above this shares the darkest colour

intensity_df <-
  intensity_rast |>
  terra::crop(zoom_ext) |>
  terra::as.data.frame(xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) |>
  data.table::as.data.table() |>
  data.table::melt(
    id.vars = c("x", "y"),
    variable.name = "ssp",
    value.name = "p_changed",
    variable.factor = TRUE
  )
intensity_df[p_changed < 0.1, p_changed := NA_real_]

map_theme <- theme_void(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    panel.spacing = unit(2, "pt"),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 7, margin = margin(b = 2)),
    legend.key.width = unit(3, "mm"),
    legend.key.height = unit(10, "mm"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 6),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 6),
    plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2)
  )

p_intensity <-
  ggplot(intensity_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = p_changed)) +
  # geom_raster, not geom_tile: ~10 M cells per figure, and tile draws one rect each.
  geom_raster() +
  facet_wrap(vars(ssp), nrow = 1) +
  viridis::scale_fill_viridis(
    limits = c(0.1, intensity_clip),
    oob = scales::squish, # clip rather than drop: >= intensity_clip is the top colour
    na.value = "#ddd",
    breaks = c(0.1, intensity_clip),
    # ASCII only: the default PNG device font has no glyph for the >= sign and silently
    # substitutes an ellipsis.
    labels = c("0.1", sprintf("%.2f+", intensity_clip)),
    name = "share of members\nallocating any change\ngrey = no change"
  ) +
  # One scale bar, on the first panel only -- five would be clutter at this size.
  ggspatial::annotation_scale(
    data = data.frame(ssp = factor(levels(intensity_df$ssp)[1], levels(intensity_df$ssp))),
    location = "bl",
    width_hint = 0.45,
    height = unit(1, "mm"),
    text_cex = 0.45,
    line_width = 0.3,
    pad_x = unit(1, "mm"),
    pad_y = unit(1, "mm")
  ) +
  coord_sf(crs = 2056, expand = FALSE, datum = NA) +
  map_theme

p_intensity

ggsave(
  "2026-05-ssp-ch/091-change-intensity-2030.png",
  p_intensity,
  width = 18,
  height = 9,
  units = "cm",
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)
```

A cell is coloured where at least 2 of the 20 members changed it, and takes the top colour where
at least 5 did. Because
the anterior map is the same everywhere, the differences between panels are attributable to the
SSP demand alone — `070`'s rate vectors are the only scenario-varying input at this horizon.

On the first real ensemble, the five scenarios separate exactly as the demand does: the expected
number of cells changing in this one decade runs from 119 k under SSP1 to 197 k under SSP5, 66 %
more. But the **envelope** — cells that change in at least one member — is 1.19–1.64 M, i.e.
29–40 % of the country and 8–10× the change that actually lands. Twenty independent uniform
draws would give roughly 20×, so the ensemble concentrates about twice as hard as chance: there is
spatial signal in the potentials, but it is soft, and a scenario's demand could be satisfied in
many more places than it needs. That is the same thing `080`'s figure of merit measures, seen
from the forward side.

> **Next step: hexbin.** At 300 dpi in an 18 cm figure one printed pixel covers roughly two
> hectare cells, so what the eye reads is a dither pattern that aliases against the pixel grid
> rather than the density it stands for. Binning the changed cells into hexagons and mapping
> **summed intensity per bin** would make the density explicit, be robust to the print scale, and
> — unlike the raster — let the full country back into the figure. The raster version stays
> useful for looking at individual patches, which is why the GeoTIFF is written.

## Where the scenarios disagree

The five panels answer "where does each scenario change things". The complementary question is
where they *differ*, which is a cheap derived layer worth having next to them: the spread across
the five scenario means at each cell. This one keeps the whole country — it is a single panel, so
there is room, and the interesting structure is regional rather than per-patch.

```{r}
#| label: alloc2030-disagreement
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 3.5
# Cell-wise across layers via terra's Summary methods, not app(): app() with an R closure
# evaluates per cell and is far too slow at 4.1 M.
disagreement <- max(intensity_rast) - min(intensity_rast)
terra::writeRaster(
  disagreement,
  "2026-05-ssp-ch/091-change-intensity-2030-disagreement.tif",
  gdal = c("COMPRESS=DEFLATE"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
disagreement <- terra::rast("2026-05-ssp-ch/091-change-intensity-2030-disagreement.tif")

disagreement_df <- data.table::as.data.table(
  terra::as.data.frame(disagreement, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
)
data.table::setnames(disagreement_df, 3L, "range_p_changed")

p_disagreement <-
  ggplot(disagreement_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = range_p_changed)) +
  geom_raster() +
  # Inferno reversed, so the ramp runs light-to-dark with increasing disagreement and reads
  # the same way round as the black-on-white panels above.
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "inferno",
    direction = -1,
    na.value = "white",
    name = "range across\nscenarios"
  ) +
  ggspatial::annotation_scale(
    location = "bl",
    width_hint = 0.25,
    height = unit(1, "mm"),
    text_cex = 0.5,
    line_width = 0.3,
    pad_x = unit(1, "mm"),
    pad_y = unit(1, "mm")
  ) +
  coord_sf(crs = 2056, expand = FALSE, datum = NA) +
  map_theme

p_disagreement

ggsave(
  "2026-05-ssp-ch/091-change-intensity-2030-disagreement.png",
  p_disagreement,
  width = 12,
  height = 9,
  units = "cm",
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)

terra::global(disagreement, c("mean", "max"), na.rm = TRUE)
```

## One map per transition

The change intensity above lumps every transition together. Split by transition, the share of
members in which a cell makes *that* transition shows where each scenario puts each kind of
change — urban growth, forest regrowth, agricultural abandonment — and is what the intervention
masks act on. Only changed cells are gathered, so the table stays small.

Each transition gets one five-panel figure of the whole country (`091-maps/`) and one GeoTIFF with
a layer per SSP. Cells below `map_threshold` are left blank: at single-member level the maps are
noise. Transitions `080` flagged as at chance should be read as such.

```{r}
#| label: alloc2030-transition-intensity
db$id_run <- NULL # read across runs
trans_intensity <- db$get_query(glue::glue(
  r"{
  with sim as (
    select id_run, id_coord, id_lulc
    from {db$get_read_expr('lulc_data_t')}
    where id_period = {target_period}
      and id_run in ({toString(members$id_run)})
  ),
  anchor as (
    select id_coord, id_lulc
    from {db$get_read_expr('lulc_data_t')}
    where id_period = {anchor_period} and id_run = 0
  ),
  member_ssp as (
    select id_run, ssp
    from {db$get_read_expr('runs_t')}
    where id_run in ({toString(members$id_run)})
  )
  select
    m.ssp,
    a.id_lulc as id_lulc_anterior,
    s.id_lulc as id_lulc_posterior,
    s.id_coord,
    count(*) / {n_members} as p_trans
  from sim s
  join anchor a on a.id_coord = s.id_coord
  join member_ssp m on m.id_run = s.id_run
  where s.id_lulc <> a.id_lulc
  group by all
  }"
))
db$id_run <- 0L

lulc_names <- db$lulc_meta_t[, .(id_lulc, name)]
trans_intensity[
  lulc_names, on = c(id_lulc_anterior = "id_lulc"), name_anterior := i.name
][
  lulc_names, on = c(id_lulc_posterior = "id_lulc"), name_posterior := i.name
][, transition := paste0(name_anterior, "_to_", name_posterior)]

trans_summary <- trans_intensity[, .(
  expected_cells = sum(p_trans),
  cells_ever = .N,
  cells_majority = sum(p_trans >= 0.5)
), by = .(transition, ssp)]
trans_summary[, total := sum(expected_cells), by = transition] |>
  dcast(total + transition ~ ssp, value.var = "expected_cells", fill = 0) |>
  setorder(-total)
```

```{r}
#| label: alloc2030-transition-maps
#| output: false
dir.create(map_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
coords_minimal <- db$coords_minimal
cell_size <- attr(coords_minimal, "resolution")
# the outline of the domain, drawn under every panel so the scattered cells have a frame
domain_outline <- terra::rast(intensity_rast[[1]]) |>
  terra::init(0) |>
  terra::mask(intensity_rast[[1]]) |>
  terra::as.polygons() |>
  sf::st_as_sf()

for (trans in sort(unique(trans_intensity$transition))) {
  trans_dt <- trans_intensity[transition == trans, .(id_coord, ssp, p_trans)]
  trans_rast <- tabular_to_raster(trans_dt, coords = coords_minimal, value_col = "p_trans")
  names(trans_rast) <- sub("^ssp_", "", names(trans_rast))
  terra::writeRaster(
    trans_rast,
    file.path(map_dir, paste0("091-", trans, "-2030.tif")),
    gdal = c("COMPRESS=DEFLATE"),
    overwrite = TRUE
  )

  plot_dt <- trans_dt[p_trans >= map_threshold][
    coords_minimal, on = "id_coord", `:=`(x = i.lon, y = i.lat)
  ][, ssp := factor(ssp, levels = scenario_runs$ssp)]
  p_trans <-
    ggplot(plot_dt, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = p_trans)) +
    # tiles, not geom_raster: only the cells above the threshold are drawn, and a raster over
    # scattered cells cannot infer the grid spacing
    geom_sf(data = domain_outline, inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey95", colour = "grey60",
            linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_tile(width = cell_size, height = cell_size) +
    facet_wrap(vars(ssp), nrow = 2, drop = FALSE) +
    viridis::scale_fill_viridis(
      limits = c(map_threshold, 1),
      name = "share of
members"
    ) +
    labs(title = gsub("_", " ", trans)) +
    coord_sf(crs = 2056, expand = FALSE, datum = NA) +
    map_theme +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 8))
  ggsave(
    file.path(map_dir, paste0("091-", trans, "-2030.png")),
    p_trans,
    width = 18,
    height = 10,
    units = "cm",
    dpi = 300,
    bg = "white"
  )
}
```
